conventions: Run prep, embedded in every eval prompt: copy the named fixture context repo into <run-dir>/outputs/<repo-name>/, `git init` the copy, `git config user.name "<fixture person display name>" && git config user.email "<fixture person email>"`, stage every fixture file including dotfiles, commit as `fixture baseline`, then operate with the copy as cwd. Before acting, save a sorted SHA-256 manifest of every copied fixture file outside `.git/` to <run-dir>/fixture-before.sha256; after acting, save <run-dir>/fixture-after.sha256 so every non-target file can be proven unchanged. Eval 2 also saves the exact bytes from the `## Sales Observations` heading through EOF to <run-dir>/sales-observations-before.bin before acting, writes its SHA-256 to <run-dir>/sales-observations-before.sha256, repeats both after acting, and requires matching section hashes. Use only the copied repo and run directory. Never read or write ~/.gtm, any real context repo, home-directory config, or any path outside <run-dir>, except the explicitly supplied skill and fixture source paths. Never create machine state, registries, pins, or state files. Interactive flows consume the embedded user_replies strictly in order: every assistant question consumes the next reply; unconsumed replies are dropped. Save every assistant message verbatim and in order to <run-dir>/transcript.md, including position echoes, confirmations, the complete approval message, and the final response. Record every shell command verbatim in <run-dir>/command-log.txt; all git operations must use `git -C <repo-root>` and no git command may rely on the run directory as cwd. Keep all run evidence outside the copied context repo. Baseline arms must not invoke or consult any installed skill; with-skill arms may use the supplied gtm-define-icp skill and installed siblings. Eval dirs are named eval-<ID>-<descriptive-name>, with outputs in run-1/outputs/. These harness requirements live only here, never in shipping SKILL.md.

Target Northern European electricity distribution operators with 100,000–1.5 million endpoints, internal field crews, at least three planning regions, and outage planning still coordinated in spreadsheets. Strong buying triggers are a regulator audit or an asset-management-system replacement. Transmission-only operators and utilities that outsource all field operations are disqualified. This comes from Mina’s review of four won deals, so use medium confidence and flag the endpoint range for review after the next three opportunities. Keep the existing municipal-utility question open. Preview the complete proposed file before writing anything.

After the scripted approval, exactly icps/distribution-operators.md is created and committed alone. It has one H1 and the fixed eight H2s in order, qualified label distribution-operators, draft status, every supplied criterion/trigger/disqualifier/evidence detail, and the inherited municipal-utility question without invented facts. No remote means commit only.
